name: Nuance DAX Copilot (Microsoft Dragon Copilot)
description: Microsoft Dragon Copilot (formerly Nuance DAX Copilot) is the enterprise-grade ambient AI documentation standard for large health systems. Powered by Azure OpenAI with deep Epic integration, it serves organizations like Mayo Clinic, Cleveland Clinic, and Kaiser Permanente. At $369-830+/provider/month (real-world $150-600 with volume), it's the most expensive option but offers unmatched EHR integration depth. Behavioral health results are reported as 'variable'—DAX was not built specifically for psychiatry and may lack native MSE structure, psychiatry-specific CPT coding, and risk assessment fields. Best fit for enterprise behavioral health divisions inside hospital systems, not solo mental health practices.
short_description: Enterprise ambient AI documentation for health systems on Epic/Cerner. $369-830+/mo list price. Behavioral health results reported as 'variable'—not built for psychiatry.
one_liner: Microsoft's enterprise ambient scribe for Epic health systems. Premium pricing, variable behavioral health results.

faqs.q: How much does Nuance DAX Copilot cost in 2026?
faqs.a: List prices as of May 2026: Per-User $1,512/month (unlimited ambient), Flex $604.80/month (base + pay-as-you-go). Real-world enterprise deals range $150-600/provider with volume. Implementation fees: $650-700 first user, $250 additional. No self-service—requires Microsoft sales.

faqs.q: Is Nuance DAX good for psychiatry?
faqs.a: Variable results reported. DAX added a mental health AI model but was not built specifically for psychiatry. May lack native MSE structure, psychiatry-specific CPT coding, and risk assessment fields. Best for enterprise behavioral health divisions, not solo psychiatry practices.

faqs.q: What's the difference between Nuance DAX and Microsoft Dragon Copilot?
faqs.a: Same product. In March 2025, Microsoft merged DAX Copilot with Dragon Medical One under the single brand 'Microsoft Dragon Copilot.' The names are interchangeable.

faqs.q: How long does DAX Copilot take to implement?
faqs.a: Typically 6+ months for enterprise deployment. Requires significant IT coordination, especially for deep Epic integration. This is a major differentiator from faster-deploying competitors.

faqs.q: Is DAX Copilot worth it for mental health practices?
faqs.a: For most mental health practices, no. The premium pricing ($369-830+/mo), 6+ month implementation, and variable behavioral health results make alternatives more practical. Freed ($39-119/mo) works for psychiatry med management. Mentalyc/Upheal ($20-120/mo) serve therapists.
